description:
## v1.2.4 - Startup diagnostics: the app now reports its own crashes

The instant crash-on-open reported for v1.2.0-v1.2.3 persisted through three signature-spoof rewrites because no device-side stack trace was ever captured. v1.2.4 adds a new default-on patch, *Startup diagnostics*, to all four supported packages (Opera, Opera Beta, Opera GX and the direct-download build):

**Self-reporting crash log**: an uncaught-exception handler is installed at Application attachBaseContext - early enough to capture provider and pre-onCreate crashes - and writes the full stack trace, thread, process name and timestamp to Android/data/<package>/files/vogelkop-diag.log, a file any file manager can open without permissions or root. The handler chains to Opera's own breakpad handler (Opera's crash flow is preserved) and re-asserts itself at every injection point.

**Startup breadcrumbs**: the log records each stage (attach-base-context, app-onCreate entered/completed), the device model, Android/SDK version, app version, which signing certificate the app currently sees for itself (Opera's vendor certificate proves the spoof engaged at runtime), and the spoof hook's own install state (ok(creator-proxy) / ok(no-creator-proxy) / failed:<throwable>). The diagnostics ship in their own extension dex and are independent of *Spoof app signature*, so a no-spoof build still self-reports.

**What v1.2.4 ruled out**: the whole pipeline was reproduced locally (official Opera 103.3.5234.91185 arm8 APK, Morphe Desktop CLI v2.1.1) and audited byte-by-byte - all 135 signature-read redirects match the merged helpers, the extension merges exactly once, every dex passes D8, native libs stay byte-identical STORED, the rebuilt manifest is semantically identical and the rebuilt resources.arsc contains the exact same entries. None of these is the crash cause; the diagnostics will pinpoint what is.

**Signing key rotated** (previous private key lost with a recycled build environment); morphe-signing.pub updated. Patch count: 9. Full history in CHANGELOG.md.
